key_insight: Introduce an embodied-world-model 'Turing Test' that measures whether video foundation models can generate future observations that humans cannot reliably distinguish from reality, revealing gaps in perceptual fidelity and robustness for downstream embodied tasks.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a human-centered, standardized evaluation to determine whether generative video/world models are both perceptually convincing to humans and robust enough for embodied AI uses (e.g., 3D prediction, interactive generation).
method: Design a human-in-the-loop Turing-style protocol where observers judge real vs. model-predicted video continuations across embodied scenarios.
Assemble a benchmark suite spanning predictive tasks and perturbations (domain shifts, sensor noise, interactive changes) and combine human judgments with automated metrics.
Analyze failure modes and robustness by measuring detection rates, perceptual fidelity, and task-relevant downstream impacts to quantify where models succeed or break.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, human-aligned evaluation framework to benchmark and improve video-based world models for embodied applications, guiding model selection and targeted robustness improvements.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the Turing-style evaluation loop showing stimulus (real vs. predicted), human judge, and outcome metrics.
Side-by-side video/frame comparisons (real vs. model prediction) to illustrate perceptual differences.
Bar chart of human detection rates and automated metric scores across models and tasks (shows gaps).
Heatmap/matrix of robustness under perturbations and domain shifts highlighting failure regions.
paper_title: Wow, wo, val! A Comprehensive Embodied World Model Evaluation Turing Test
paper_authors: Chun-Kai Fan, Xiaowei Chi, Xiaozhu Ju, Hao Li, Yong Bao
